clue.text: Each part of this clue, say

definitions.text: Each part of this clue, say

blocks.clueFragment: Each part of this clue, say
blocks.note: surface reading: a request to name or describe the pieces of the clue
setter's reading: every word in the clue is said in a single beat, so each is an example of the answer

explanation.walkthrough: Every word of the clue (each, part, of, this, clue, say) has one syllable, so 'say' marks them as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: A word pronounced in just one beat of sound is the technical term here, and each clue word qualifies.

clue.text: Painter puts capital into factories

indicators.note: 'puts into' means placing one thing inside another, so the first item sits within the second

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, and capital is old slang for excellent; the 1 is written as the letter I
mills are factories, such as cotton mills

explanation.surface: An artist investing his money in industrial works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money or a city, but it is the old exclamation 'Capital!', meaning A1. AI goes into MILLS: MILL(AI)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Everett Millais was a Victorian artist and a founder of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood.

clue.text: Interchangeable fertilizer

indicators.note: something changeable can alter its form, so the letters before it may be rearranged

blocks.note: the first five letters of this word are the fodder; the rest of it is the instruction

explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'Interchangeable' splits in two: the first part is the letters and the rest says they can be changed around.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, saltpetre, a compound long spread on fields to feed crops.

clue.text: Food produced by wise race

blocks.note: sage as an adjective means wise
the Derby is the famous English horse race at Epsom

explanation.surface: A meal said to be cooked up by a clever people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like a people or nation, but it is a horse race. Sage Derby is an English cheese marbled green with sage leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a hard English cheese flavoured with herbs, and cheese is eaten, so it counts as an item of nourishment.

clue.text: Advanced fast

blocks.note: first meaning: handed over money as a loan
second meaning: the Christian season of abstinence before Easter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Advanced fast' reads as 'moved forward quickly'; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that is advanced has been loaned out, and the forty days before Easter are a period of religious fasting.

clue.text: Old language reappears as modern Arabic dialect

blocks.note: taken as written
Syrian Arabic is the variety spoken in Syria today

explanation.surface: An ancient tongue resurfaces in the speech of a present-day Arab country.
explanation.walkthrough: The ancient name is simply the two words run together: the old tongue reappears as AS + SYRIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Assyrian is the ancient Semitic tongue of Assyria, recorded in cuneiform and long extinct in that form.

clue.text: Italy can be an ordeal . . .

definitions.note: the sense runs on into 7-down: the lay people, in contrast with the one clergyman there

indicators.note: 'can be' says the word before it may become something else, so its letters are free to be rearranged

blocks.note: the name of the country, taken as written
not part of the wordplay: the newspaper scan copied these words from the clue to 24-down

explanation.surface: Musing on what Italy might turn out to be, a thought continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Warning: 'an ordeal' is a scan error copied from 24-down; the printed wording is lost. This clue and 7-down read as one: Italy's lay people, but a clergyman in church.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are ordinary church members who are not ordained clergy, the contrast drawn with the minister in the following clue.

clue.text: . . . but there's one in church here

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a minster is a large church, as in York Minster

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: unlike lay people, here is one person inside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis follows on from 6-down, the lay people; this clue supplies the contrast, a clergyman. A minster is a great church such as York Minster.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman serving a congregation is a member of the clergy, the opposite of the lay people in the previous clue.

clue.text: Lighter daughter rudely pushed

blocks.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl less heavy than her sister shoved her way past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like a comparative of light, or a cigarette lighter, but it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge is to shove or force one's way roughly into people, so the past tense means shoved impolitely.

clue.text: Many a sitting may be arranged for them

indicators.note: to arrange things is to put them in a new order, so the letters are shuffled

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a crossword way of saying many
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plenty of court sessions may be scheduled for these people.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as a description: court sittings are arranged for the parties to a lawsuit, so 'them' points back across the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties to a lawsuit are the people for whom court sessions are scheduled, so the pronoun stands for them.

clue.text: Small island business — a Spanish one

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for island
biz is informal shorthand for business, as in showbiz
taken as written

explanation.surface: A little island enterprise, owned by a Spaniard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small island' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies only the abbreviation; the definition is 'Spanish one', meaning a Spanish island.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean, belonging to Spain and famous for holidays.

clue.text: Things to do for a male or female group, say

indicators.note: 'say' asks us to speak the phrase aloud and listen to how it comes out

blocks.note: males and females are each a gender, so one of them is a gender

explanation.surface: A to-do list drawn up for men or for women.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'a gender' and the list word are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, as at a meeting, so it is a set of tasks.

clue.text: Gee! Two fish in one

blocks.note: gee is the spelt-out name of the letter G
first fish: the ray, a flat sea fish
second fish: the ling, a long relative of the cod

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at finding two fish rolled into one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gee!' looks like an exclamation, but it is the letter. 'One' refers back to fish: the answer is a fish itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater game fish of the salmon family, so it is one more fish alongside the other two.

clue.text: Number of swans swimming round river — this one?

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: 'seven swans a-swimming' is a line from the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Counting the swans gliding about a river, and asking which river it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The carol The Twelve Days of Christmas has 'seven swans a-swimming', which supplies the number; 'this one?' asks which river the swans are on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is Britain's longest river, so it is the river in question, where swans might well be swimming.

clue.text: Architect whose wife was provoked

blocks.note: surface reading: a building designer with an annoyed spouse
setter's reading: points to the Restoration comedy The Provok'd Wife, written by this architect who was also a playwright

explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Vanbrugh designed Blenheim Palace and Castle Howard, and also wrote the play The Provok'd Wife (1697).
explanation.definitionFit: He is a baroque designer of English country houses who also wrote comedies, one titled after a provoked wife.

clue.text: Religious leader and Edward talked colloquially

blocks.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A rabbi and his friend Edward had a chat.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering at length, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' = talk.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British speech, to rabbit means to chatter on, so the past tense is a slang word for having talked.

clue.text: Ostracize from jet set over dance

blocks.note: jet black: jet is a deep black stone
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Shunning someone from the fashionable international crowd over a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet set' reads as the rich travelling crowd, but 'jet' is the colour and 'set over' places it above the second piece in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To blackball someone is to vote to exclude them from a club, so it means to shut them out socially.

clue.text: Times unfair in this period?

blocks.note: fair can mean light in colour, so its opposite is dark
ages are long times or eras

explanation.surface: A complaint that life was unjust back in those days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfair' looks like 'unjust', but it is the opposite of fair-haired or pale. The pieces come in the reverse of clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: The early medieval era in Europe is traditionally called by this name, so it is the historical stretch the clue asks about.

clue.text: Worker giving help to many, perhaps

indicators.note: 'perhaps' hints the word could be some other form of itself, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to give someone a hand is to help them
taken as written

explanation.surface: An employee who lends assistance to lots of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' suggests the word many could take another form, so its letters are rearranged after HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman is a person employed to do odd repair jobs, so he is a kind of labourer.

clue.text: Lid for container? Just the opposite

definitions.text: Lid for container? Just the opposite

blocks.note: surface reading: a cover to put on a box or jar
setter's reading: a lid is slang for a hat, so swap it round to a container for a hat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lid' is slang for a hat; the answer is a box for holding a hat, the reverse of a cover for a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A round box made to store headwear is exactly a receptacle for a lid in its slang sense.

clue.text: Growing incentive

blocks.note: first meaning: a root vegetable that grows in the garden
second meaning: a reward dangled to motivate

explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing incentive' reads as an increasing reward. 'Growing' stands for something that grows, a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange root vegetable grows in the soil, and the idiom 'carrot and stick' makes it a reward offered for motivation.

clue.text: Despite her anxiety, withdraw capital

indicators.note: read as with-draw, it says to draw letters out from within the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of Despite, all of her, and the start of anxiety

explanation.surface: Someone nervous decides to pull out of a trip to a city.
explanation.walkthrough: TEHERAN is an older spelling of Tehran, the capital of Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran, also spelt Teheran, is the seat of government of Iran and its largest city.

clue.text: Way for Americans to transform old weapon

blocks.note: to turn something into something else is to transform it
a pike is a long spear once used by infantry

explanation.surface: An American method of converting an antique arm into something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' looks like a method, but it is a road.
explanation.definitionFit: In the United States a turnpike is a toll motorway, so it is a road used by Americans.

clue.text: The beast has got both of father's letters

blocks.note: pa is father; this is the first of its two letters
both X and Y: the word that joins the two letters
the second letter of pa

explanation.surface: An animal that owns its dad's correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: Both of the letters of PA, said as 'P and A', run together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a black and white bear of China, so it is an animal or creature.

clue.text: Beginning of stage craft seen in short play

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of stage
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: Theatre skills on show in a brief drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage craft' reads as theatrical skill, but 'craft' is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a brief comic scene in a revue or comedy show, so it is a little drama.

clue.text: Probation can be an ordeal

blocks.note: first meaning: a test period
second meaning: a painful experience

explanation.surface: Being on probation is hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Probation' suggests the criminal sentence, but here it means testing someone out.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is both a test period before acceptance and a painful testing experience, like the old trial by ordeal.

clue.text: Greek character used to disturb game, we hear

indicators.note: 'we hear' means the answer is judged by its spoken sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: a beater drives grouse or pheasants out of cover towards the guns

explanation.surface: A Greek person employed to flush birds on a shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is a letter, not a person. In a non-rhotic British accent beater and the letter name sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter or symbol of Greek writing.

clue.text: Mouthpiece for instrument

blocks.note: first meaning: a newspaper or journal speaking for a party or group
second meaning: the keyboard instrument with pipes, as in a church

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouthpiece for instrument' sounds like the part of a trumpet you blow into; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's official newspaper is called its organ, and the pipe organ is a large musical instrument.

clue.text: Re-reading order for old soldier

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters get a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: Instructions to go over a text again, issued for a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a military command, which suits the soldier, but it means put the letters into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadiers were originally soldiers who threw grenades, and later a regiment of tall infantry, so a historic fighting man.

clue.text: Post-war aid scheme spoils house design

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil, so mars is spoils
a hall is a large country house
a plan is a design or drawing

explanation.surface: An aid programme after the war wrecks an architect's drawing for a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like a noun, the spoils of war, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The American programme of 1948 named after George Marshall funded the economic recovery of Western Europe.
